moduleTitle: Extracting SMS messages using email service in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Distinguish Testim-managed email inboxes from direct SMS retrieval.
Use permanent/temporary addresses and supported email filtering/export.
Explain the documented CLI/Twilio SMS retrieval path and separate it from an independently configured forwarding scenario.

elements.description: Testim’s managed email feature creates permanent inbox addresses in Settings > Email Service or temporary addresses through Generate email address. Third-party providers are not used to generate these managed addresses; that is not a ban on all external-service integrations.

Validate email reads managed-inbox messages for coded checks or codeless filters. The codeless mode can extract text/links and exposes emailData, emailExtractedText and emailExtractedLinks. Generic DOM Extract Value is not required to read that inbox.

bulletPoints: Permanent and temporary managed inboxes use different creation paths.
Validate email provides filtering and exports; do not assume generic DOM extraction reads inbox messages.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Email and SMS are separate retrieval paths

elements.description: Use the managed inbox for supported email flows. Match the intended message and required outcome rather than assuming any message proves the current request succeeded.

The official Extract SMS message example uses a CLI action with Twilio, sender/recipient filters, recent-message checks and a returned Promise. It exports the code from the selected message. This is an SMS-provider path, not the managed email inbox.

elements.text: Forwarding SMS content into email is an independent environment-specific alternative only if explicitly configured and verified. It does not prove SMS delivery to a phone and is not certified here as the original Academy workflow.

bulletPoints: Email content uses Validate email filtering/export.
Direct SMS retrieval has a documented CLI/Twilio path.
Configured forwarding is an independent alternative, not a general SMS/email equivalence.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Selecting and reusing the required message value

elements.description: Filter for the intended message, verify required content and export the code/link with supported scope. Extracting one value does not replace message assertions or prove phone delivery. Avoid assuming the first old mailbox message belongs to the current test.

elements.term: Choosing permanent vs. temporary for this scenario
elements.description: Use a reusable permanent inbox or per-run temporary inbox according to the email scenario. A fresh inbox does not create a fresh phone number or guarantee a newly registered backend account.

bulletPoints: Assert the intended message and export the required value.
Fresh email inboxes and fresh phone/account state are separate requirements.

examPitfalls.title: Treating managed email as the only SMS path
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Claiming Testim has no documented direct SMS integration.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Distinguish managed email validation from the CLI/Twilio SMS example. Forwarding requires separate setup and validation.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing extraction with delivery coverage
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating an exported code as proof of every required delivery/content behavior.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Validate the intended recent message, required content and application outcome; phone delivery is separate from an email-forwarding check.

examPitfalls.title: Treating a temporary inbox as a new phone
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Generating an email and assuming it also creates unused SMS recipient/account state.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Set up phone/account state separately. Temporary inbox generation supplies an email address, not a phone number.

options.text: A third-party email provider Testim connects to for generating test addresses.
Testim's own built-in mechanism for generating and reading email addresses/messages — permanent (via Settings) or temporary (via a test step).
A paid add-on unrelated to test steps.
A feature that only works with Gmail accounts.

practiceQuiz.hint: Scope the answer to managed email inboxes.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The managed inbox feature generates permanent and per-run temporary email addresses. Its provider restriction applies to those addresses; external SMS-provider CLI integrations are a separate feature.

optionExplanations.A: The described managed-address feature uses Testim’s service.
optionExplanations.B: Testim supplies managed permanent and temporary inbox addresses.
optionExplanations.C: Managed validation is connected to supported test steps.
optionExplanations.D: The service is not restricted to Gmail accounts.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How is a permanent Testim email address created?

options.text: Settings → Email Service → Generate Email Address.
By adding a Generate email address step inside the test.
Permanent addresses aren't supported — every address is temporary.
By connecting an external email provider's API key.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's a one-time setup action, not a per-run test step.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A permanent email address is created once, from Settings → Email Service → Generate Email Address. A Generate email address STEP inside a test instead produces a fresh, temporary address on every run — the two are distinct mechanisms.

optionExplanations.A: Settings > Email Service generates the permanent address.
optionExplanations.B: The test step generates a temporary address per run.
optionExplanations.D: External provider credentials do not create Testim’s managed permanent address.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which documented path retrieves SMS messages directly, rather than assuming they were forwarded to email?

options.text: Because Testim cannot handle SMS in any form.
A CLI action using Twilio, message filters and an exported code.
Because SMS messages are always identical to emails technically.
Because Testim's email service physically sends SMS messages.

practiceQuiz.hint: Managed email and SMS-provider retrieval are separate paths.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The official SMS example uses a CLI action with Twilio and exports a code after filtering messages. Generic DOM Extract Value does not directly read an SMS-provider inbox.

optionExplanations.A: The documented CLI path can retrieve SMS messages.
optionExplanations.B: The documented example uses a CLI/Twilio action and message filtering.
optionExplanations.C: SMS and email are distinct delivery channels.
optionExplanations.D: Managed email does not physically send SMS messages.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An email signup scenario needs a generated inbox for each run. Which address creation path supplies that inbox without also claiming to create a fresh phone number?

options.text: A permanent address, reused every run.
A temporary address, freshly generated on each run via a Generate email address step.
Either works identically for this scenario.
Neither — this scenario isn't supported by Testim's email service.

practiceQuiz.hint: The scenario explicitly needs a fresh, unused contact point each time.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Generate email address supplies a per-run temporary inbox. Phone numbers and backend account state need separate setup; the generated email alone does not certify them.

optionExplanations.A: Reusing a permanent inbox does not satisfy the per-run inbox requirement.
optionExplanations.B: The temporary-address step generates a per-run inbox.
optionExplanations.C: The creation/lifetime choices are distinct for this requirement.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A codeless Validate email step has matched the intended message. How can later steps reuse its extracted code or link?

options.text: Extracting values is not actually supported for forwarded messages.
Use supported emailExtractedText or emailExtractedLinks exports, with appropriate scope and assertions.
Assume a generic DOM Extract Value step automatically reads every inbox.
The step cannot export matched message content.

practiceQuiz.hint: The email validation step provides its own text/link export parameters.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented codeless email step provides text/link exports. Assert required message behavior separately; exporting a code does not prove every delivery/content requirement.

optionExplanations.A: The codeless email step supports content extraction.
optionExplanations.B: These documented exports provide extracted text/links for later supported usage.
optionExplanations.C: DOM extraction does not automatically retrieve arbitrary inboxes.
optionExplanations.D: The documented email step exposes extracted content.

quickRecap.value: Managed email addresses are created by Testim; this does not prohibit separate SMS-provider integrations.
Settings > Email Service generates a permanent inbox address.
Generate email address supplies a per-run temporary inbox, not a new phone/account.
Official direct SMS retrieval uses a CLI/Twilio action; forwarding is separate environment setup.
Validate email can filter messages and export text/links; extraction does not replace outcome assertions.
